answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying below it, draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4 (discarding 4), and draws 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I; Animals goes in the leftmost slot (strength 1) and the other four are randomly placed in the remaining slots. Starting appeal is staggered by turn order: 0 for the start player, then 1, 2, and 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C3: 1 association worker ... active ... remaining 3 lying down; D: Take 25 money; E: Draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 ... B: Animals card under the leftmost slot ... remaining 4 randomly ... side I; C1: Appeal ... start player on space 0, second ... 1, third ... 2, fourth ... 3.

answers.answer: Four-player setup places the top 4 Base Conservation Projects face up below the Association board; two- and three-player setups place 3. In a two-player game only, unused-color tokens block the left level of the left card, middle level of the middle card, and right level of the right card, plus the three spaces in the left column of the donation area. The summary gives no blocked spaces for three or four players. The initial six-card display is revealed after everyone has chosen their hand cards.
answers.evidence: In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up ... otherwise the 3 topmost; 2-player game only ... cover ... levels ... and ... three spaces in the left column of the donation area. After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were to its left one slot to the right, and put the used card in slot 1. Action strength is fixed before the action; each X-token spent beforehand adds 1 strength, and tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. You may spend any number, but may never hold more than 5 X-tokens. An after-finishing effect occurs after the action is complete, including the Action-card movement.
answers.evidence: After completing the action, remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1. You set the strength before performing the action ... X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action. ... 'after finishing' ... complete the action — including moving the Action cards.

answers.answer: You may not do nothing as a regular action. The alternative is to choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right. Its slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: You may not do nothing ... Use the alternative X-token action ... If you cannot or do not want to perform any of the 5 actions, take exactly 1 X-token instead. You must still select an Action card, move it to slot 1 ... If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.

answers.answer: Reaching the last Break-track space triggers a break after the current turn ends and grants the player who reached it 1 X-token. Ignore movement beyond the last space. The player completes the rest of the current turn before the break; after the break, play continues clockwise with the next player. A normal break alone does not grant extra turns.
answers.evidence: When it reaches the last space, you call a break ... after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token ... Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. ... Play then continues clockwise with the next player. A normal break alone does not give any extra turns.

answers.answer: Both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. On side I, choose either a deck draw per the table (maximum 3 cards, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card of any reputation; snapping does not include a deck draw. On side II, draw from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order per the upgraded table, or snap exactly 1 display card at strength 3+; strength above 3 adds nothing to a snap. Snapping is unrestricted by reputation on either side; the reputation restriction applies to side-II display draws. Display cards taken during the action are replenished only at turn end. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard down to the hand limit at breaks.
answers.evidence: CARDS side I ... advance ... 2 spaces ... draw from the deck ... or snap ... strength 5 or more ... exactly 1 ... regardless of your reputation. ... side II ... draw cards from the deck and/or from within reputation range ... snapping ... strength 3 ... On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw ... display is not replenished until your turn is complete ... discard to your limit during breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. Above reputation 15, the counter stays at 15 and you gain 1 appeal per additional reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: 'Within reputation range' = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action ... on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take 1 appeal per remaining reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building whose size is no greater than action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in that action. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. Your first building must include at least one map-border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. Build only on empty spaces and cannot cover water or rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately grants 1 appeal, once.
answers.evidence: Side I: Build exactly 1 ... size up to ... Pay 2 money per space ... first building ... border ... Placement rules ... adjacent to an existing building ... restricted icon require upgraded Build ... kiosk ... at least 3 spaces ... Each pavilion ... increases ... appeal by 1. Side II: as many different buildings ... maximum total size equal to strength ... never 2 identical.

answers.answer: Build I allows standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary (each size 5). The supply has four tiles of each special-enclosure type, and each zoo may have only one of each type. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Buildings table lists Petting Zoo as Build I and Reptile House/Large Bird Aviary as Build II; supply has four tiles of each special enclosure ... each individual zoo ... only one of each type. Unique buildings can never be built with this action ... if you cover every space except water and rock ... immediately gain 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes. Money, cards, and newly activated workers gained earlier in an action can be used in later steps of that same action. Pay for each item before receiving that item's benefits. Immediate effects resolve when they occur; after-finishing effects wait until the entire action, including Action-card movement, is complete. If effects are simultaneous, the player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps ... You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. ... 'After finishing' ... complete the action — including moving the Action cards ... If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.

answers.answer: To play an animal, meet every left-side condition, pay its cost, and place it in a legal empty enclosure. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon on that card, so a double continent icon gives a 6-money reduction. An animal may use an empty standard enclosure at least as large as required; the enclosure flips to its occupied side and normally houses one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may instead use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if they fit; mark the required spaces with player tokens, and do not flip the special enclosure. Required water/rock adjacency applies to the chosen housing; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes. Resolve ordinary effects immediately (including before a second animal), but defer after-finishing effects until the action ends; choose the order of simultaneous effects.
answers.evidence: For each animal: check conditions; pay cost; partner zoo ... reduces ... by 3 money per continent icon; fill an empty enclosure ... at least the required size ... flip ... Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo ... special enclosure ... mark ... spaces ... water/rock requirements apply ... Effects ... immediately ... 'After finishing' effects wait ... If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.

answers.answer: Animals II adds the option to play animals from the display within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; hand and display animals may be mixed, and the display is not replenished until turn end. At strength 5+, gain 1 reputation first, at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies. It also permits animals with the upgrade-required condition icon.
answers.evidence: Side II ... play Animal cards from the display within your reputation range, paying an additional cost equal to the folder number ... display is not replenished until your turn ends. ... strength 5 or more ... first increase your reputation by 1 — at the very beginning ... may also play animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.

answers.answer: When building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary with Build II, you may immediately move all suitable animals that fit from standard enclosures, choosing separately for each animal. The summary says special-enclosure admission is marked with player tokens for the number of spaces used. It does not specify how transferred animals' capacity is marked, which standard enclosure is flipped empty, or any fallback rule for choosing an enclosure to empty.
answers.evidence: When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately ... move all suitable animals that fit from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. The animal-admission table says special enclosures use player tokens to mark the number of spaces shown; no transfer or vacated-enclosure procedure is given.

answers.answer: The four Association tasks have strengths 2 (increase reputation), 3 (gain partner zoo), 4 (gain university), and 5 (conservation-project work). Association I performs exactly one task; Association II can perform one or more different tasks whose total value is at most action strength. A worker is required for each task: use 1 if you have no worker on that task, 2 if you already have 1 there, and you cannot do it again before the break if you have 3 there. Other players' workers do not matter.
answers.evidence: Side I ... exactly one ... at least 1 active worker ... if 1 ... already on that task, ... 2 ... if 3 ... cannot ... until after the break. Other players' workers ... do not matter. Task strengths are 2, 3, 4, 5. Side II ... one or more different ... total value ... may not exceed ... strength.

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from available tiles on the Association board and placed on the lowest available matching space on the zoo map; take any printed bonus immediately, and gain university reputation if shown. Association-board stocks replenish at breaks so each tile is available once, skipping tiles all players already have. Partner zoos must be from different continents, with a maximum of 4; the third or fourth requires Association II. Universities cannot be duplicated, and they are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5.
answers.evidence: Gain partner zoo ... take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty ... space ... printed bonus immediately ... all ... different continents, maximum 4 ... third (or fourth) requires upgraded Association. Gain university ... take ... onto the lowest available ... take any printed bonus; advance ... if ... reputation ... cannot take a duplicate ... Universities ... only way to increase hand limit to 5. Break: replenish ... so each is available exactly once.

answers.answer: With Association I, project work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. Association II can also play a new project from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. Support a project only once per player, and only use a reward level with no player's token on it; place one of your left-edge zoo-map tokens on a condition you fulfill. Removing that token activates its map bonus immediately, taken before or after the project reward. Above-board projects are limited to 2, 3, or 4 by player count; an excess new project replaces/discards the rightmost card, and any tokens on that discarded card return to their owners' supplies, not their maps. Base projects remain in place.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work ... support ... or play ... from your hand and support it immediately. Side II ... play ... from the display ... paying the folder number. A reward level is available only if no player ... has a token ... normally may support a particular project only once ... place 1 player token ... from the left edge ... Taking a token off ... activates its bonus ... immediately ... card limit ... discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies ... Base ... never moved.

answers.answer: A Release into the Wild project requires discarding an animal with the specific icon whose printed standard-enclosure size matches the project's size exactly, even if it could also live in a special enclosure. You first lose only its printed appeal, then discard it and lose its icons. You retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure, remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or, if none does, the smallest occupied one meeting size alone. If no occupied enclosure meets size, flip none.
answers.evidence: The animal must require a standard enclosure of the depicted size ... match exactly, not smaller or larger. First lose only the animal's printed appeal ... discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects ... If ... could live in a special enclosure, first remove ... tokens if possible; only otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level, or instead advances the Break token by strength and grants that much money. Sponsors II plays one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their combined levels; cards may come from hand or from the display within reputation range, with the folder number paid as extra cost. Resolve cards in sequence, fully resolving each instant effect (except after-finishing effects) before the next card. The side-II money option advances the Break token and pays twice the strength in money. On side I, the full strength amount of money is paid even if only one Break-track step remains.
answers.evidence: Side I ... exactly 1 Sponsor ... strength ... at least ... level. OR advance ... steps equal to strength and take that much money — full money even if ... doesn't need all the steps. Side II ... one or more ... strength +1 ... sum of levels ... hand or display ... paying folder number ... Play them one after another ... instant effects ... before the next. ... money twice.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the relevant university); return tokens on Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, move remaining cards down and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Kiosks earn 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, while empty special enclosures do. Income is appeal-based money, then kiosk income, then break-icon income on Sponsors and activated map bonuses. If multiple players take display cards during break income, process them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), refilling the display after each player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 list hand limit, tokens, workers/Association board, display, income, and track reset. Kiosk income lists adjacent buildings and occupied standard enclosures ... empty special enclosure does. Income order is appeal, kiosk, Sponsor/map break income. Display cards: resolve affected players clockwise ... refill after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token at that space. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before the end, everyone discards one before scoring. Check for game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn ends or a break, unless someone triggers the end sooner. The triggering player completes their turn, then all others take one final turn; if triggered during a break, every player takes one final turn. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation points. Victory points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; ties go to the player with most supported projects, then are shared.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: 2 points gives upgrade or worker; 5 and 8 gives 5 money or Bonus token; first time any player reaches 10, all discard one Final Scoring card. End check ... at end of your own turn or during a break ... same scoring area, or pass ... gains on another player's turn wait ... triggering player completes ... others one more turn; during break all players ... Final Scoring card maximum 4 ... VP = Appeal value − Target Number ... tie: most conservation projects, then shared victory.
